prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the passenger in a rear-end collision in Pasadena, Texas, and has wrist fracture. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1439; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement concerns the rear-end collision you were involved in as a passenger in Pasadena, Texas. Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd rather just keep it to the accident details, if that's okay.

Q: That's fine, we can note that you prefer not to state your name at this time. Can you describe where you were seated and what you were doing just before the impact?

A: I was in the front passenger seat. The driver and I were stopped at a light on a city street, waiting to turn.

Q: Did you notice the other vehicle before the collision?

A: Not really. I heard tires behind us and then a hard jolt from the back. My head snapped forward and then back.

Q: Did you feel any immediate pain or injury at the scene?

A: My neck hurt right away, and my left wrist was throbbing. I didn't think much of the wrist at first because I was mostly worried about my neck and my back.

Q: Did you seek medical attention, and if so, when?

A: The ambulance took me to the emergency room that same evening. They took X-rays and said the wrist was fractured. They put me in a splint and told me to see a specialist.

Q: Have you been seeing that specialist since?

A: Yes, I've had two follow-up visits. I'm wearing a cast now and I've had trouble gripping things, so I've been relying on my family for everyday tasks.

Q: Thank you. Is there anything else you would like to add to your statement?

A: Only that I'm still recovering and I'd like the claim to reflect the fracture and the time I've missed from work.

Q: Understood. This concludes the recorded statement. Thank you.

A: Thank you.
